entities.summary:
Anaxarchus was a Greek philosopher of the school of Democritus who accompanied Alexander the Great into Asia, fostering the spread of skeptical thought. 

Born in the 4th century BCE, Anaxarchus' philosophical views emphasized the limitations of knowledge and the importance of individual experience. 

Together with Pyrrho, he traveled extensively with Alexander, exploring the ancient world and developing a nuanced understanding of the human condition. 

Anaxarchus' philosophical legacy extends beyond his contemporaries, influencing later skeptical thinkers such as Sextus Empiricus and shaping the development of Western philosophy. 

In the annals of history, Anaxarchus' contributions serve as a testament to the enduring power of intellectual curiosity and the human quest for knowledge.
